summary: The earliest parseably dated released-corpus hit names Rød-Larsen on 2010-05-04; preserved routed/dyadic content begins in September 2010, not by 1999.
detail: On May 4, 2010 Epstein told staff to call an initially unnamed UN contact, then asked for his full name; staff replied 'Terje Roed-Larsen' and scheduled a call for May 5. The corpus does not prove the call occurred. The earliest preserved outbound routing instruction is EFTA01811325 on September 28, and the earliest preserved incoming content from Rød-Larsen's office is EFTA02418985 on September 29. No valid pre-May-2010 internal date survived underlying-document review. This late terminus does not update H3 because the released corpus is left-censored; it only means pre-committed rule 2 did not fire.

summary: Juul first appears contextually in March 2011, while the only direct Epstein↔Juul thread found contains three messages dated 2018-04-21.
detail: Epstein referred to 'mona and the kids' in a March 22, 2011 message to Rød-Larsen, and a March 27 travel-administration email is the earliest full-name occurrence. target_name: Jeffrey Epstein and Terje Rød-Larsen correspondence
summary: Across 1,986 confirmed correspondence document IDs from 2010-2019, 22 hit retrospective terms, six carried third-party material about the 1993 channel, and zero contain Epstein credit-taking for an Oslo role.
detail: A high-recall 2,322-ID candidate envelope was narrowed to 1,986 canonical IDs with a confirmed Epstein/Rød-Larsen From-To header pair or explicit relay. The slice spans 2010-09-28 to 2019-03-18. Twenty-two documents hit at least one pre-committed retrospective term. Six refer to the 1993 channel: two 2013 anniversary-op-ed forwards, three 2016 play-review forwards, and one 2018 anniversary-article forward. All six are third-party content sent by Rød-Larsen or his office; none is an Epstein statement about his own role or a pre-1993 relationship. This within-coverage silence triggers pre-committed rule 5 and significantly updates toward H3, while not proving that no earlier contact occurred.

summary: Epstein-linked funds supported an IPI-hosted private Oslo performance and play-labeled contributions, but the reviewed evidence does not establish that Epstein financed or produced the underlying theatrical production.
detail: Epstein wrote contemporaneously that he had anonymously bought out the entire Vivian Beaumont theatre so UN diplomats could see Oslo. KPMG's later review of IPI's ledger and supporting records identified a $150,000 Gratitude America donation described as 'Reimbursement of tickets to the Oslo Play' and a separate $100,000 contribution described as 'Oslo Play'; KPMG found no donor instructions restricting the contributions. Official Playbill/IBDB credits name Lincoln Center Theater as producer and do not name Epstein. The evidence supports funding the May 5 ticket buyout/private performance and related IPI costs or contributions, not production financing.
